mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the 3-month periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL y/y exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month increase in both employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals an overheating economy that triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST increase by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL y/y > 3.0%), a decline in the federal funds rate signals the central bank's preemptive action to prevent economic contraction, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL y/y > 3.0%), the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in recessionary risks.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the 3-month periods where INDPRO declines by at least 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 1.0% over the prior 3 months, it signals a contraction in consumer demand for housing, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST declines by at least 1.0% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in employment (PAYEMS) over the prior 3 months signals a tightening labor market that fuels wage inflation, leading to expectations of prolonged monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE is below 4.0% and PAYEMS grows by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle economic expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% y/y), a decline in residential sales (RSAFS) by more than 1.0% over the prior 3 months signals a weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 y/y > 2.5%), the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS declines by at least 1.0%.
